newsitem.title: SPAIN: MOTORCYCLING-CRIVILLE OUT FOR REVENGE OVER DOOHAN.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-CRIVILLE OUT FOR REVENGE OVER DOOHAN.

text.p: Home favourite Alex Criville seeks revenge over world 500cc motorcycle champion Michael Doohan in Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix after being controversially beaten by the Australian in last year's race.
Criville's fans were already celebrating victory in the 1996 event when their hero fell, handing Doohan a victory that ultimately proved decisive in lifting his third world title.

The Spaniard had been able to hold off Doohan until the final lap of a thrilling race, but let the Australian through on the penultimate curve after slowing to avoid jubilant fans who had spilled onto the track.
Criville fought desperately to get back on the final bend, only to crash within sight of the finish.
Spanish security chiefs are taking special measures this season, including extra barriers and officials, to control the expected crowd of more than 100,000 at the circuit on a holiday weekend.

With Honda riders Doohan and Criville dominating the first two races this year - the Australian won with the Spaniard second in both Malaysia and Japan - Sunday's grand prix looks set to be another close duel.
Doohan is proving wrong the doubters who thought he might not have what it takes to stay on top of the category for a fourth consecutive season.
The champion has also surprised his rivals by taming a more radical and less smooth engine which gave him the edge in Malaysia.
The race in Japan two weeks ago ended with Doohan just a few bike lengths ahead of his rival after a dramatic head-to-head confrontation.
"Even in Spain I wouldn't have won, I was at the limit," said Criville afterwards.
Spanish fans hope that will not be the case this weekend, when they will also be cheering for Carlos Checa, who beat off both Criville and Doohan to win the Catalan Grand Prix last September.
